title: Geometric syntax
tagline: the grammars streets and buildings are written in
summary: How each street stands in the whole, its choice and its integration, beside the walkers counted. A grammar learned from any place's streets by compression — what repeats, up to rotation, scale and position, becomes a rule — and played back on the map step by step; another place parsed by it; streets that were never drawn sampled from it, freely or within their context; blocks and buildings read as words of triangles. The syntax analyser parses structures and triangulations and saves every grammar, derivation and parse.

layers.title: the grammar of the streets
layers.about: Pick a place: its streets become a geometric graph, a grammar is learned from it, and its derivation plays on the map. Then parse another place by it, or sample streets from it.

layers.title: blocks and buildings as words of triangles
layers.about: Pick a place: its blocks or its buildings' footprints are triangulated, each triangle a letter by its angles; the grammar of their gluing, and a patch grown from it.

layers.title: how each street stands in the whole
layers.about: Pick a place: its streets within 1.5 km are read as a whole, each coloured by its choice or its integration (Space Syntax) at an angular, metric or topological cost and a radius. In Melbourne, the City's counters stand beside them at their mean daily walkers.

tools.title: The syntax analyser
tools.about: Grammars learned from self-similar structures and grids, their derivations played step by step, turned copies parsed by them; triangles rewritten by Pachner's, the midpoint's and Sierpinski's moves, and their derivations recovered from the final triangles.

source: Ways and buildings: Overture Maps, OpenStreetMap. The grammars: syntaxis (ADR 0083); configuration: urban-science on morphe's centralities (ADR 0084), after Hillier and Hanson (1984), after Fiser, Benes, Garcia Galicia, Abdul-Massih, Aliaga and Krs (2016), Learning geometric graph grammars; urban-science's and architecture's syntax.
